findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed a member of staff to dump liquid down hand sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used to wash hands.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no paper towels to be present at the front or back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to both hand sinks. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: (Repeatx3) Observed sections of the counters in the front house area to be held together by duct tape. Duct tape is not an approved materiel for construction in food service. Discussed repairs with PIC, tape will be removed and counters will be repaired. Areas shroud be smooth, easily cleanable, and non absorbent.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
(Repeatx2) Observed no food handlers licenses to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, staff will all take the steps to receive license this week. Ensure any employee that handles food has completed the required food handlers training after 3 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed an employee put on gloves without washing hands. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff is washing hands before applying fresh gloves.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed a bucket to be sitting in the back handwashing station sink by office. Discussed with PIC and relocated. Ensure hand washing stations are kept easily accessible so handwashing is encouraged.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed the back hand sink near triple sink to not have any paper towels available. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were restocked. Ensure hand washing stations are fully equipped to maintain proper hand washing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sani bucket to be 100 ppm. Inspector asked the employee to re-make the sani bucket. 200 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Ensure sani buckets are frequently changed in order to maintain appropriate concentrations. Quat: 200-400 ppm. Utilize test strips to verify concentration. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

Observed an open bottle of Comet sitting on a shelf above food contact utensils and bowls. Discussed with PIC and relocated. Ensure potentially poisonous materials are stored below or away food contact surfaces.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed coffee stir sticks to be sitting in a soiled container. Discussed with PIC and cleaned. Ensure food contact utensil storage is cleaned at a frequency to prevent soiling.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Observed multiple utensils and pots to be accumulating food debris on the shelving left of the triple sink. Discussed with PIC. Ensure equipment is stored and cleaned at a frequency to prevent contamination before use.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple sample spoons to not have handle facing upward. Discussed with PIC and replaced. Ensure single service utensils are stored in a way to prevent contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed food debris behind the lid of the prep cooler. PIC is instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain the area clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The walk in cooler fans have a thick accumulation of dust. The situation was discussed with the PIC.  Clean prior to the next routine inspection and maintain clean moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
Sections of the counters in the front house area are being held together with duct tape. Duct tape is not an approved material for construction in food service. Areas should be repaired so counter is not fraying or coming away and tape is not longer used. Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure areas are corrected before next routine inspection. Areas should be smooth, easily cleanable, non-absorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple locations throughout the facility are in need of cleaning during this inspection. Areas include: 1) the ceiling tiles around the air intakes; 2) floors into corners and under shelves. PIC is instructed to clean these area and maintain them clean moving foreword.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler’s licenses for employees. Ensure all staff has an active food handler’s license. Valid for 3 years. Ensure copies are left at the facility. Discussed with PIC. Employees should have a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment.
